34.t: Ory band lineup, Les Hite tour east, six years with Liggins
34.s: With Hite from 1939 he went to New York and Boston until wartime, then spent about six years with Joe Liggins; he now plays only occasional gigs.
34.ch: Kansas City, Chicago and California bands
34.q: Piano player, yeah. Ed Garland on the bass, Minor Hall on the drums, Ory, and myself. I played up there with them for a long time. And then I left that and I went with Les Hyde, a big band.

251.t: Hall leaves the band; the Cincinnati breakup and social security card
251.s: Hall left for a year, rejoined, and stayed in Cincinnati when the band broke up; his card shows 1938.
251.q: And... ...the man. I mean, you got to remember the Hawk. You stole everything, man. Now we could find out who the Hawk was.

841.t: Playing with Vincent Lopreston's band in Homer
841.s: Harris adds a note about four weeks with an Italian leader's band outside the city, with McCullough, O'Connell and Teddy Johnson.
841.q: From New Orleans. New Orleans. George McCollum was playing trumpet and Willie O'Connell was playing, uh, things like that. I mean, I had Teddy Johnson playing alto too. Oh, Teddy, yeah. Yeah, Teddy, he was playing. Well, we only had two altos at that time. That had been alto. Yeah, he's playing…

825.t: Joining Herbert Leary's big swing band, 1935-41
825.s: Around 1935 Ernie joined Herbert Leary's big band and stayed until 1941, then returned to Dixieland. The band stayed local with short trips such as Baton Rouge.
825.ch: Big bands, Depression work and the WPA band
825.q: Well, not too much. Well, I mean after around 1935, that's when I joined Herbert Larry's big swing band then. I stayed with him from... Well, then there's a side of Singapore. Yeah, I joined him from 35 to 41. I stayed with him. And after that then I went back to playing Dixieland music again.

1.t: Joining Benny Carter's 1938 band and staying sharp
1.s: As Russell's band broke up, Barker joined Benny Carter's 1938 band and stayed visible around Harlem, then played with Logan, Baron Lee and Billy Fowler and got stranded in North Carolina.
1.q: No. Meantime Paul and Red Allen . . . Red Allen’s getting ready to go on his own and go with Fletcher Henderson and Pops Foster. They getting ready to break up the Luis Russell band. Everybody’s scattered around. I’m playing with all these bands, and there’s Benny Carter.

406.t: Cab Calloway offers him a job at the Hippodrome
406.s: While he played drunk at a club, Cab Calloway offered him a place. Thinking it a joke he did not show up, until Doc Cheatham and Walter Thomas told him Cab was serious.
406.ch: Zach White, Cotton Pickers and Cab Calloway
406.q: So one night we were playing over to one of -- we had a friend there named BAILEY that owned (unintelligible) two or three places. And we were over there playing this night and Cab Calloway's band was playing at the Hippodome Theater. And I, that night I was standing up in a chair half juiced,…

379.t: Subbing at the Cotton Club and being hired by Cab Calloway
379.s: He subs for Doc Cheatham at the Cotton Club and Cab then hires him on salary, the best-paying band.
379.q: Then Doc Cheetam is the first trumpet player (inaudible). So he got sick. They had a big production, and they needed somebody to come in there and (inaudible).

70.t: Calloway's offer at the Adams Theater and the uniform tailor
70.s: Chu Berry tells him Calloway wants him; at the Adams Theater in Newark Calloway hires him, and the band's uniforms come free from the tailor Carnik.
70.q: And Choo Choo Berry was sitting in the lobby. So Choo Choo Berry told me, he said, 'Say, Brother,' he said, 'Calloway wants to see you.' And I said, 'Yeah?' And he said, 'Yeah,' he said, 'come over to the Adams Theater tomorrow.'

7.t: Straw boss and the notice rescinded by Mills
7.s: Thomas explains how he got his notice and Mills ordered it rescinded.
7.q: and... Because see, Cab, when we decided to stay with the band, I guess he got the idea to change to different musicians. So I guess I was next on the list. So I didn't think too much about it. I kind of hated to leave the band, because it was beginning to do good. So next time Cab and I went…

455.s: Budd joins Calloway in Chattanooga replacing Rudy Powell, praises the organization, and gets a pink slip at the Capitol Theater.
455.ch: Cab Calloway, Haiti and Sarah Vaughan
455.q: Oh, yes. Calloway's band. Well, you know, Cab sent for me to come down there, and it was in 1947. And I joined you in Chattanooga, Tennessee.
